reason: buildPendingBody sets isStatic:false; flipping to true makes the phantom body static, and the test asserts id/position/velocity but never isStatic, so a proper assertion would catch it.

Math.PI/12 vs *12 changes the spread angle in buildImpulseVelocity's direction branch, altering velocity x/y; the test only calls buildPendingBody without a direction and asserts magnitude, so the direction branch is untested.
dx/dist vs dx*dist changes the normalized direction vector and thus the computed spawn position for distinct entities with dist>1, which is observable and uncovered.
hasSufficientResources returns false on the no-state path which a test can pin with toBe(false); undefined would fail such an assertion, so it is a real gap in the attributed suite.
if(entry)->if(true) in debitResources makes a payload key missing from state dereference entry.value on undefined and throw, observable by debiting a key absent from state.
if(!state)->if(true) makes hasSufficientResources always log an error and return false even when resources are sufficient, which a happy-path test would catch.
if(!isRecord(value))->if(false) skips the early return in stripDefinitionStateKeys so a null value reaches Object.keys(null) and throws instead of returning a clone.
returning undefined instead of structuredClone(value) for non-record entries makes saveStateEntry yield undefined so saveState drops primitive-valued state keys that were previously preserved.
||->&& in clearTransientDraft's guard means a truthy non-object draft (e.g. a string) is no longer skipped and gets rebuilt into the default draft, an observable difference no test exercises.
restorePassportPermanentEntries returns the issues array; returning undefined breaks callers that read .length or iterate, and the path is uncovered.
===->!== in resolveParentId inverts the entity_id branch, resolving the wrong parent id (or falling through), which is observable for entity_id parents and uncovered.
if(parent.kind==="entity_id")->if(true) forces every parent through the entity_id branch, skipping the tag-based fallback for tag parents, observable and uncovered.
returning undefined instead of issue(...) when restorePhysicsBody fails makes the entry count as successfully restored, changing the returned issues list; uncovered.
!==->=== inverts the layer guard in syncPhysicsBody so a defined serialized.layer is no longer applied (and undefined is), observable by restoring a body with a specific layer.
>->= at resolvedCommands.length>MAX_COMMANDS_PER_TICK changes behavior at exactly MAX, throwing fatal where the original passes; a boundary test at MAX distinguishes them.
safeDt<=0 vs <0 differs only at safeDt===0, which normalizeDt actually produces for dt<=0/non-finite, so dt<=0 returns null vs proceeding with a zero timeStep; boundary is reachable and uncovered.
if(payload.isImmediate!==true)->if(false) makes TRANSFER_ASSETS never set entityListChanged for non-immediate transfers, an observable summary difference that is uncovered.
arrivals.length>0 vs >=0 makes the guard effectively always-true (length is non-negative), so an empty arrivals set with pending commands would reprocess commands where the original skips it.
refreshSnapshotPhase returns snapshot.reset(...); returning undefined breaks runtimeSnapshotBuffers which assigns and uses that Snapshot, an observable regression.
arrivals.length>0 becoming >1 changes behavior when exactly one arrival plus pending commands occur, skipping the reprocess the original performs.
>->= at projectedTotal>MAX_COMMANDS_PER_TICK throws overflow at exactly MAX where the original allows it; a boundary test at MAX distinguishes them.
if(dt<=0)->if(true) makes the phase always return early with empty commands so no systems ever tick, a gross observable change that is uncovered.
activeCount:0->1 in the AutomationSnapshot initializer offsets the reported active count by one, observable by asserting activeCount when no automations are active; uncovered.
if(!blueprintId)->if(true) forces an early undefined return so blueprint-sourced buffs are never resolved for entities lacking own buffs, observable with a blueprint-only-buffs entity.
The 10 is the starting hp value in a test fixture whose action SET-writes value:100; since SET ignores the current value, changing 10 to 11 does not alter the asserted output.
if(...)->if(false) removes the non-string/empty guard so a non-string NaN-coercible ActionValue reaches value.trim() and throws instead of returning 0, observable with such input.
if(action.target.startsWith("self.powerSink."))->if(true) routes every mutate action to executePowerSinkMutation regardless of target, a gross observable change that is uncovered.
if(target.entityId==="sys_world")->if(false) skips the SET_GLOBAL branch so a sys_world target emits a state mutation instead, an observable command-type difference; uncovered.
caveIndex+1 vs -1 checks the element before 'cave' instead of after, so a valid x.cave.attributes.* target no longer matches 'attributes' and returns null; observable and uncovered.
normalizeTruthiness returns value>0 for numbers; returning undefined yields a falsy non-boolean so a positive number returns undefined instead of true, catchable via toBe(true).
